manuscript_statement: For a law with memory the second law restricts the relaxation function and the entropy flux, not only the signs of the coefficients (Coleman and Gurtin 1967; Chen and Nunziato 1974).
source_wording_max25words: When q/theta is regarded to be a flux of entropy due to heat flow
what_source_actually_states: The paper treats materials with internal state variables whose evolution obeys ordinary differential equations. The second law enters as the Clausius-Duhem inequality (3.2), which restricts the response functions (free energy determines stress and entropy). The entropy flux is not derived or restricted: it is taken as q/theta by assumption in (3.1). The paper contains no relaxation function of a memory law; fading memory is named only as a different theory (p.597).
notes: Source confirms DOI on its first page (10.1063/1.1711937). The statement attributes two specifics to this source (relaxation function; entropy flux restricted by the second law); neither is in the paper. Supersedes batch 001, where the source was unavailable.

manuscript_statement: For a law with memory the second law restricts the relaxation function and the entropy flux, not only the signs of the coefficients (Coleman and Gurtin 1967; Chen and Nunziato 1974).
source_page_or_equation: printed p.795, Theorem 1; printed p.797, Theorem 2
what_source_actually_states: Theorems 1 and 2 derive from the dissipation inequality that the energy relaxation function and the heat-flux relaxation function satisfy beta(0) >= 0, alpha(0) >= 0, alpha'(0) <= 0 and that the equilibrium conductivity is non-negative. The paper says nothing about the second law restricting the entropy flux; the entropy and the heat flux are fixed by the free energy through (2.13), and the restrictions obtained are on the relaxation functions only.
notes: Relaxation-function part is supported (indeed stronger than 'signs of coefficients': inequalities on functions). Entropy-flux part is not in the source. No DOI printed on the scanned first page; DOI left as '-' because none was verified here.

manuscript_statement: For a law with memory the second law constrains the relaxation function itself, including its initial value and slope (Chen and Nunziato 1974).
source_page_or_equation: printed p.795 Theorem 1(ii); printed p.797 Theorem 2; printed p.798 Abstract
source_wording_max25words: the initial slope of the heat flux relaxation function is non-positive
what_source_actually_states: Theorem 1 gives alpha'(0) <= 0 and beta(0) >= 0; Theorem 2 gives alpha(0) > 0 (non-negative in the Abstract). The Abstract lists the three results: initial values of the energy and heat-flux relaxation functions non-negative, initial slope of the heat-flux relaxation function non-positive, equilibrium conductivity non-negative.
notes: Direct support, with one precision: the initial slope condition is stated for the heat-flux relaxation function alpha; the energy relaxation function beta gets only an initial-value condition. Supersedes batch 001, where the source was unavailable.

manuscript_statement: The Green-Naghdi type-II law is lossless, as it should be for a theory without energy dissipation (Green and Naghdi 1993).
source_page_or_equation: printed p.202 (after eq (3.17)); also p.200 and p.198
source_wording_max25words: permit propagation of harmonic waves without damping
what_source_actually_states: For thermoelasticity type II the paper states that (3.7) and (3.9) involve an absence of internal rate of production of entropy so that there is no dissipation of energy (p.200), that type II 'involves no dissipation of energy' (p.198), and that under c > 0, kappa* >= 0, lambda + 2mu >= 0 the system (3.15)-(3.16) permits propagation of harmonic waves without damping (p.202).
notes: Now read on the pages missing from batch 001 (p.202 supplies the explicit 'without damping' wording). The source does not use the word 'lossless'; the equation-level statement is 'without damping'. DOI from library filename suffix, not printed on the scan.

manuscript_statement: The Green-Naghdi theories use an entropy flux different from q/T0.
source_wording_max25words: the internal flux of entropy k (= h/theta)
what_source_actually_states: Item (2.16) gives h = theta k and (2.17) defines the entropy flux vector p through q = theta p, so in the boundary conditions the internal flux of entropy is written k = h/theta (p.203). The flux is thus the heat flux divided by the temperature theta, not by the reference temperature theta0. To first order in the linearized type I theory p = -(kappa/theta0) grad theta ((2.38)3, p.197), which is q/theta0; for type II the flux follows from the Pi-derivative of the free energy ((3.13)3, p.201) instead of a Fourier law. The manuscript sentence therefore holds for the general theory and for type II, but not as a difference visible in linearized type I.
notes: Keeps batch 001's PARTLY SUPPORTED verdict and adds the pages it lacked (p.201 (3.13)3, p.203). The literal phrase 'different from q/T0' does not occur; support is inferential, from q = theta p and from the flux being fixed by the free-energy potential. The theta versus theta0 distinction should be reported to the authors, not smoothed over.
